title: validate_record output
description: Output for validate_record. `valid` is the verdict; `issues` is EVERY violation the extraction path's validator found, not the first one, so a caller fixes all of them at once; `record` is the validated record as plain JSON when valid and null when it is not. A schema the engine's grammar cannot express is REFUSED as an error rather than reported here, because that is a fault in the caller's schema, not a verdict about the record.

valid.description: Whether the record is admissible under the caller's schema, judged by the same validator an extraction uses.

issues.description: Every violation found, as path-qualified strings. Empty exactly when `valid` is true.

record.description: The validated record, copied into plain JSON, or null when the record is invalid. Null rather than absent so a caller never has to distinguish 'no record' from a dropped property. The record's own fields are governed by the caller's schema, not by this envelope: the host's schema DSL cannot advertise `additionalProperties` on a union-typed node, so it is deliberately not repeated here (structured_extract's output schema has the same shape for the same reason).

allOf.description: A negative verdict carries no record: there is nothing admissible to return.
A positive verdict carries no unresolved issue. JSON Schema cannot correlate two fields without this conditional, and the code enforces the same rule directly.

meta.description: The host stamps this envelope. The provider never authors it (EXT-17).
